description: SpaceMiT K1 / X60: 8x riscv64, VLEN=256 (zvl256b), two 4-core clusters distinguished by their L2 domain. Everything here was measured on the board, not read off a datasheet -- see artifacts/k1_bringup/*/ in the XPU-RT checkout.

notes.clusters: cores 0-3 share one 512K L2, cores 4-7 share another (cpu_freq_cache.txt: index2 lvl=2 Unified 512K shared=0-3 / shared=4-7). /proc/cpuinfo reports an identical ISA on all 8 harts and never mentions IME, so the split is not discoverable that way.
notes.ime: smt.vmadot EXECUTES on cores 0-3 and TRAPS on cores 4-7, established with a per-core SIGILL probe repeated three times (ime_capability_probe.txt). An IME kernel on cluster 1 does not degrade, it dies -- so the capability list below is a correctness constraint, not a performance hint.
notes.ime_reachability: Declared here because the hardware has it. Note that as of artifacts/k1_run/ime_gate/FINDINGS.md no CONVOLUTION can reach the matrix engine through the current compiler: every xsmtvdot hook is matmul-only, and the one vmadot observed in DroNet was a 1x1x2048 GEMV padded up to the mandatory 4x4 tile with 15 of 16 lanes discarded. Treat ime_* capabilities as available-in-principle until a conv path exists.
notes.clock: cores are pinned to the `performance` governor at 1.6 GHz; there is a single cpufreq policy with related_cpus 0-7, so the clusters CANNOT be clocked independently. rdcycle raises SIGILL from userspace; rdtime is unprivileged and runs at a fixed 24.000 MHz (device-tree timebase-frequency = 24000000). Timing MUST convert with 24 MHz, never the 1.6 GHz core clock.
notes.rvv_symmetry: measured cluster-1/cluster-0 median ratio 0.996 on compute-bound dispatches -- the two clusters are equivalent for RVV, so placement across them is a scheduling choice rather than a performance one.
notes.contention: measured co-runner slowdown is 1.043x same-cluster vs 1.185x cross-cluster. That is the OPPOSITE of the shared-L2 intuition and means 'spread across clusters' is the wrong default on this board.

cores.name: cluster0_core0
cores.description: Cluster 0, L2 domain 0. Carries IME (smt.vmadot) in addition to RVV.

cores.name: cluster1_core4
cores.description: Cluster 1, L2 domain 1. RVV only -- smt.vmadot traps here. No ime_* capability, deliberately.
